newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZOLA AND BECKHAM LIGHT UP PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZOLA AND BECKHAM LIGHT UP PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: At the start of this season, few people outside Manchester had heard much of David Beckham and few soccer fans in England had significant interest in Gianfranco Zola.
Since then, as Saturday's clash between Chelsea and Manchester United confirmed, the two men have emerged as the brightest lights in the English game.
Newcastle's Alan Shearer and Arsenal's Ian Wright are vying for the prize of the premier league's top scorer but that is nothing new.

The wonderful thing about the emergence of Beckham at United and the blossoming of Zola at Chelsea since his arrival from Parma just three months ago is that neither was expected -- at least not this season.
The Italian's artful second minute goal in the 1-1 draw drew ample praise from United manager Alex Ferguson.
"Of all the teams we have met this season Chelsea showed the most imagination in the final third of the field," he said. "Zola is even better than I thought he was."
"I thought I could push my full-backs forward but he was clever enough to go and play out wide. He has got a very good head on him."
And Gullit said players of the calibre of Zola and Beckham were illuminating English football like never before.
"The premier league is getting better. It is becoming an example abroad, and I can say this because I have played there," he said.
Zola's goal was truly imaginative, albeit that he was aided by sloppy United defending.

The Italian latched on to a pass down the right flank from Dan Petrescu, took the ball to the touchline, fooled fullback Denis Irwin, strolled past a leaden-footed Gary Pallister and beat Peter Schmeichel on his inside post with embarrassing ease.

In contrast, Beckham's strike was about power and timing. Gary Neville swung in an innocuous looking cross from the right, Chelsea defender Eddie Sinclair headed the ball skywards, and when it fell Beckham crashed home a crisp volley off the underside of the bar.
It has been a productive week in the capital for United, who confirmed themselves as favourites to defend their title last Wednesday when they beat Arsenal at Highbury.
Not so good for Chelsea, who, after letting slip a 2-0 lead in the F.A. Cup at Leicester, travelled to Zola's homeland and lost to AC Milan in a friendly before rushing back to London to face United.
With hindsight, their Italian jaunt may have cost them a couple of league points on Saturday.
"We looked very tired in the second half. It's not an excuse but getting back at four a.m. (on Thursday) didn't help," captain Dennis Wise said.
United had no such worries and, after a hesitant start, seemed to gain in strength as the match progressed.

That has been the pattern of their season and their current form -- they have not lost a league match since November 2 when Chelsea beat them at Old Trafford -- looks ominous for England's other title contenders.
